answer: Each new agent has to pass a live latency check: a verifier sends a nonce from three regional nodes and wants a signed reply within 40 ms, so every identity proves it's a separate machine at a specific location. A farm in a shale-country data center can't put 500 keys on one copper uplink, because replies from shared hardware show the same timing signal and get clustered together. Each fake needs its own host in a different place, about $6 a month, and the checks come back at random times. So the bill grows by one server for every key you add.
